previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: The patient was admitted with persistent nausea, epigastric pain, dry heaves, and inability to maintain adequate oral intake for over a week. She has a history of gastric bypass and prior gastric erosion. On admission, she was started on IV fluids, pantoprazole, and anti-nausea medication. Due to malnutrition, a PICC line was placed on hospital day 2, and TPN was initiated and gradually advanced without complications. An EGD on day 5 revealed mild gastritis and a small hiatal hernia, with no ulceration. Pantoprazole was increased to 80 mg twice daily per gastroenterology recommendation. The patient's symptoms improved, she tolerated a stage 5 bariatric diet, and was discharged home on nocturnal TPN and IV pantoprazole with plans for outpatient follow-up in gastroenterology and surgery. Cyclic vomiting syndrome was suggested as a possible contributing diagnosis.
problems: Unspecified gastritis and gastroduodenitis, without mention of hemorrhage
Diaphragmatic hernia without mention of obstruction or gangrene

Discharge Instructions:
You were admitted to the hospital for placement of a gastrostomy 
tube by Interventional Radiology for transition from TPN to tube 
feedings, which has been successful.  You are now tolerating 
your goal TF rate and your PICC has been removed.  You are now 
preparing for discharge to home with the following instructions:

-Some discomfort around the tube site is normal for the first 
few days after surgery.  If you experience severe, worsening 
pain, fever > 101.5°, nausea or vomiting, call your physician. 

-The tube will be ready for use ___ days after it is inserted.  
Your physician ___ discuss the appropriate timing for 
initiation of feedings.

-If the tube is not in use, you may place the provided cap over 
the outside opening and secure the tube to your abdomen with 
tape. 

-Please look at the site every day for signs of infection 
(increased redness or pain, swelling, odor, yellow or bloody 
discharge, warm to touch, fever).

-Wash the area gently with warm, soapy water.

-Keep the insertion site clean and dry otherwise.

-Avoid swimming, baths, hot tubs; do not submerge yourself in 
water.

-Make sure to keep the drain attached securely to your body to 
prevent pulling or dislocation.

-Additionally, please call your doctor or nurse practitioner or 
return to the Emergency Department for any of the following:
*You experience new chest pain, pressure, squeezing or 
tightness.
*New or worsening cough, shortness of breath, or wheeze.
*If you are vomiting and cannot keep down fluids or your 
medications.
*You are getting dehydrated due to continued vomiting, diarrhea, 
or other reasons. Signs of dehydration include dry mouth, rapid 
heartbeat, or feeling dizzy or faint when standing.
*You see blood or dark/black material when you vomit or have a 
bowel movement.
*You experience burning when you urinate, have blood in your 
urine, or experience a discharge.
*Your pain in not improving within ___ hours or is not gone 
within 24 hours. Call or return immediately if your pain is 
getting worse or changes location or moving to your chest or 
back.
*You have shaking chills, or fever greater than 101.5 degrees 
Fahrenheit or 38 degrees Celsius.
*Any change in your symptoms, or any new symptoms that concern 
you.
Please resume all regular home medications , unless specifically 
advised not to take a particular medication. Also, please take 
any new medications as prescribed.

Please get plenty of rest, continue to ambulate several times 
per day, and drink adequate amounts of fluids. Avoid lifting 
weights greater than ___ lbs until you follow-up with your 
surgeon.
Avoid driving or operating heavy machinery while taking pain 
medications.

radiology_notes.text:
PERCUTANEOUS G-TUBE PLACEMENT

INDICATION:  ___ woman with history of obesity, status post Roux-en-Y
gastric bypass with dumping syndrome, malnutrition on TPN.

OPERATORS: Drs. ___ (fellow), ___ (resident) and
Dr. ___ physician). Dr. ___ was present throughout the
procedure.

CONTRAST:  Sterile 15 mL Omnipaque 300.

SEDATION:  Moderate sedation with divided doses of 100 mcg of fentanyl and 2
mg Versed over 75 minutes, during which the patient's hemodynamic status was
continuously monitored by a trained radiology nurse.

OTHER MEDICATION:  IV 1 g cefazolin and IV 0.5 mg glucagon.

PROCEDURE AND FINDINGS:  Consent was obtained after explaining the benefits,
risks, and alternatives.  Patient was placed supine on the imaging table in
the interventional suite.  Timeout was performed as per ___ protocol.

A ___ feeding tube was placed via the left nostril with its tip
in the gastric remnant, under intermittent fluoroscopic guidance.  About 60 mL
of gas was insufflated.  Limited sonographic guidance was performed in the
epigastrium to assess for the margin of the left lobe of liver.  A radioopaque
marker was placed at the site of old G-tube.  3D DynaCT was performed to
confirm the anatomy.  The patient was then prepared in a sterile fashion. 
After infiltrating the skin and subcutaneous tissues with adequate amounts of
1% lidocaine, a micropuncture needle was placed at the site of old
percutaneous G-tube, and with its tip likely in the gastric lumen.  A 0.018
wire was advanced through the needle and coiled within the gastric bubble. 
The needle was then exchanged for 4 ___ microsheath after making a small
incision at the access site.  Inner cannula and wire were removed to place a
0.035 short ___ wire, which was advanced into the lower esophagus. 
Microsheath was then exchanged to place a 5 ___ ___ sheath.  After
removing the inner cannula, a small amount of sterile half-strength contrast
material was injected through the sidearm to confirm position within the
gastric lumen.  After removing the sheath, the tract was dilated with a 9
___ dilator.  Eventually, a 12 ___ peel-away sheath was placed, with its
tip in the gastric lumen.  After removing the inner dilator, a trimmed 12
___ ___ G-tube was placed within the sheath, which was then
peeled away.  While gently withdrawing the string, the G-tube was slowly
pulled out to form the retention pigtail loop in the gastric lumen. A small
amount of sterile half-strength contrast material was injected to confirm
position.  Tube was then cleared with sterile saline.  String was locked. 
Catheter was secured by 0 silk sutures and Flexi-Trak.  Site was dressed
appropriately.  Patient tolerated the procedure well and no immediate
post-procedure complication was seen.

Incidental note of gastroesophageal reflux to the mid thoracic esophagus was
made.
